chapter: Becoming a musician: ukulele, clarinet and the Boozaire Kings
title: Never gambling; Milt loses at cards in Cab Calloway's band
summary: Danny lost money shooting dice once and never gambled; Milt recalls losing to Illinois Jacquet and Russell Smith in Cab's band.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Now, as far as me going through [t'rou] my money, I'd never gamble, because I lost my money once shooting dice with some kids. This little cat could shoot dice, and I didn't know, I just wanted to be a smart-aleck, and he just won my money. I don't know how to shoot dice until today. I never did like gambling. I can give you some money, but I ain't into gambling. I never had that lustful feeling about it.
You know I went through that. I lost every dime I had in Cab's band. Then I finally got hip and quit.
Yeah. Who used to do all that winning up there when you all'd be gambling?
Oh, Illinois Jacquet and those guys. Ike Quebec. Jacquet was always winning.
Russell Smith was cheating. When he'd play cards, poker, he used to stick cards all up his sleeve.
